title: Miso Soup
subtitle: Japanese dashi broth with white miso and tofu
excerpt: A light Japanese soup of dashi broth stirred with white miso paste, soft silken tofu, and wakame seaweed. Ready in 10 minutes and deeply restorative.

recipe.sourceNotes: Miso soup (misoshiru) is one of the most fundamental dishes in Japanese cuisine, consumed daily by many Japanese households at breakfast, lunch, or dinner. It consists of a dashi stock base with miso paste dissolved into it and various ingredients added according to season and preference. Dashi is a light stock made by steeping kombu (dried kelp) and katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes) in water; a vegan version uses only kombu and is called kombu dashi. White miso (shiro miso) has a milder, sweeter flavour than red or brown miso (which are fermented for longer) and is the most common everyday choice. Silken tofu and wakame seaweed are the most traditional additions. The critical rule of miso soup is that the miso is never boiled once added: boiling destroys the beneficial bacteria in the miso and diminishes the flavour.

content.text: Never boil the soup after the miso has been added. The miso is stirred in at the very end once the pan is off the heat or the heat has been reduced to the lowest setting. Dissolve the miso paste in a small amount of the warm dashi first before adding it to the pan: this prevents lumps. Silken tofu is very delicate and will break up if stirred; add it to the pan and let it warm through gently without agitation.

items.preparation: soaked in cold water for 5 minutes, drained

content.text: Make the dashi: put the kombu in a saucepan with 1 litre of cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer over medium-low heat. Remove the kombu just before the water boils. For a richer dashi, steep the kombu for 30 minutes in the cold water before heating.
Add the tofu and drained wakame to the warm dashi. Heat gently until the tofu is warmed through. Do not boil. Remove from the heat or reduce to the lowest setting.

Put the miso paste in a small bowl. Scoop a ladleful of warm dashi into the bowl and whisk until the miso is fully dissolved. Pour back into the pan and stir gently. Taste and add a dash of soy sauce if more depth is needed. Ladle into bowls and scatter with spring onion. Serve immediately.
